source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 16: moment about Q(4, 2, 2) of F = -2i + j - 3k acting at P, r = QP (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312: 15i - 15j - 15k.

blocks.prompt: 16. A force \(\underline{F} = -2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\) is applied at \(P(-1, -3, 2)\). Find its moment about the point \(Q(4, 2, 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
A moment-of-force question.
We must find the moment (a vector) of \(\underline{F}\) about \(Q\).
Plan: \(\underline{r} = \underline{QP}\), then \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) by the determinant.
steps:
Given: force \(\underline{F}\) acting through \(P(-1, -3, 2)\); point \(Q(4, 2, 2)\).
To find: the moment of \(\underline{F}\) about \(Q\).
Method: Moment \(= \underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) (14.3.7 (c)), where \(\underline{r}\) is the vector from the point \(Q\) (about which we turn) to a point \(P\) on the line of action of the force. The force is given in components.

Write the force
\[\underline{F} = -2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\]
Why: Its components are the rows we need in the determinant.

Find \(\underline{r} = \underline{QP}\)
\[\underline{QP} = (-1 - 4)\underline{i} + (-3 - 2)\underline{j} + (2 - 2)\underline{k}\]
\[= -5\underline{i} - 5\underline{j}\]
Why: \(\underline{r}\) starts at the point \(Q\) about which the moment is taken and ends at the point \(P\) where the force acts.

Write the determinant
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ -5 & -5 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{r}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{F}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-5)(-3) - (0)(1) = 15\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (-5)(-3) - (0)(-2) = 15\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (-5)(1) - (-5)(-2) = -15\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \underline{i}(15) - \underline{j}(15) + \underline{k}(-15)\]
\[= 15\underline{i} - 15\underline{j} - 15\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Magnitude of the moment
\[|\underline{r} \times \underline{F}| = \sqrt{(15)^2 + (-15)^2 + (-15)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{675} = 15 \sqrt{3}\]
Why: The length tells how strong the turning effect is.

Check
\[(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}) \cdot \underline{F} = (15)(-2) + (-15)(1) + (-15)(-3)\]
\[= -30 - 15 + 45 = 0\]
Why: The moment \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) must be perpendicular to \(\underline{F}\) (and to \(\underline{r}\)); the dot product is 0.
